क्या आप जानते हैं कि हमारे चहेते Harry Potter यानी Daniel Radcliffe यह आइकॉनिक रोल लगभग गंवाने ही वाले थे? 🧙‍♂️

रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक, BBC की डॉक्यूमेंट्री David Copperfield में 10 साल के Daniel को देखकर डायरेक्टर Chris Columbus उन्हें इस रोल में लेने के लिए बिल्कुल तैयार थे। 🎬

लेकिन The Telegraph की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, शुरुआती शर्त के तहत Daniel को 6 फिल्मों का कॉन्ट्रैक्ट साइन करना था और शूटिंग Los Angeles में होनी थी। Daniel की मां ने इसे उनकी पढ़ाई और लाइफ में बहुत बड़ा डिस्टर्बेंस माना और ऑफर से साफ मना कर दिया। ❌

फिर एक थिएटर्स प्ले के दौरान प्रोड्यूसर David Heyman की नजर Daniel पर पड़ी। उनकी गहरी नीली आंखों और शांत स्वभाव ने David का ध्यान खींच लिया और उन्होंने पेरेंट्स से दोबारा बात की। 🎭

Warner Bros. ने अपनी शर्तें बदलते हुए Los Angeles के बजाय United Kingdom में सिर्फ 2 फिल्मों का नया ऑफर दिया। पेरेंट्स के राजी होने के बाद Daniel ने स्क्रीन टेस्ट दिया और वो बन गए सबके चहेते विजार्ड! ⚡

ctx.title: Daniel Radcliffe Almost Missed His Chance To Become Harry Potter Over One Condition From His Parents
ctx.summary:
Daniel Radcliffe almost missed his chance to play Harry Potter because of one condition his parents set. Know why his parents denied. 
 The post  Daniel Radcliffe Almost Missed His Chance To Become Harry Potter Over One Condition From His Parents  appeared first on  Koimoi .
ctx.text:
No matter how many adaptations of Harry Potter come out, there won’t be any Harry like Daniel Radcliffe, wearing those round glasses. As an 11-year-old, Radcliffe looked perfect as the little wizard.
But you’ll be surprised to know that he once almost lost the opportunity to join the franchise, and that too, because of his parents. The reason behind Radcliffe’s parents was not a failed audition or competition with another actor.
In fact, according to GQ , director Chris Columbus was convinced that Radcliffe was the perfect choice for Harry Potter after watching him in the BBC documentary David Copperfield. So, what made his parents turn down the offer?
At the age of 10, Daniel Radcliffe made his debut in the industry with a BBC documentary, David Copperfield , back in 1999. Columbus, who was then preparing to direct the first two Harry Potter movies, immediately believed that he had found the right one.
However, when the filmmakers approached Radcliffe’s parents, Alan and Marcia, they didn’t want their son to take up the role, according to The Telegraph . Their problem was not with the role but with conditions that came along with it.
Radcliffe later revealed that the original deal required him to sign on for around six films, all of which were supposed to be shot in Los Angeles. Radcliffe’s mom saw this as way too hectic and said, “That’s too much disruption to his life. That’s not gonna happen.”
As a result, Radcliffe’s chances of playing Harry Potter seemed to be almost over. But fate and Hollywood had other plans for him.
Later that year, Harry Potter producer David Heyman and Steve Kloves attended a play in London. And, coincidentally, Radcliffe happened to sit directly beside them, according to Entertainment Weekly . Heyman instantly recognized him and became more interested in watching him than the play.
Heyman said, “All I was thinking about was the boy sitting in the row behind me – Daniel Radcliffe. He had these big blue eyes, a deep curiosity, a real stillness and composure – he was an old soul in a young body.”
The meeting convinced Heyman to talk to Radcliffe’s parents again. This time, he managed to reconsider them while Warner Bros. also made some changes to the original deal.
Instead of a six-film commitment in Los Angeles, the studio offered Radcliffe a two-film contract in the United Kingdom. The revised agreement addressed his parents’ concerns, and finally, Daniel Radcliffe screen-tested for the role of Harry Potter, aka the Boy Who Lived.
